title: The Borwein–Bailey–Girgensohn series conjecture
statement:
Let $S_{\mathrm{BBG}}$ denote the Borwein–Bailey–Girgensohn series, let $M=\log 6$, and write $S_{\mathrm{BBG}}=M+R$. For $t>0$, define the exponential integral by

$$
\operatorname{Ei}(t)=\gamma+\log t+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{t^n}{n\cdot n!},
$$

and set $\mathrm{li}(x)=\operatorname{Ei}(\log x)$ for $x>1$.

**Main conjecture.**

$$
S_{\mathrm{BBG}}=\operatorname{Ei}(\log 3)=\mathrm{li}(3)\approx 2.163\,588\,594\,667\,192\ldots
$$

Equivalently, $R=\operatorname{Ei}(\log 3)-\log 6\approx 0.3718\ldots$.

The exact identity $M=\log 6$ is unconditional, so the conjectural content concerns the remainder $R$. If true, this would give a notable appearance of the logarithmic integral in a trigonometric series with integer arguments.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14548

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).
source_name: Carlos Lopez Zapata, “Bessel Averaging, Fourier Decomposition, and the Value of the Borwein-Bailey-Girgensohn Series”, arXiv:2603.14548 (2026).
